description: Preguntas a Jev (TypeSafe) en las puertas del arnés (hsdd_nucleo.pregunta_jev). Una Choice por puerta entre los verbos que no piden texto y «persona» (que lo decida una persona). Jev nunca escribe un motivo, así que nunca rechaza ni pide cambios: solo puede dar por buena una puerta o devolverla a una persona. El estado es {puerta: {tipo, titulo, texto}, opciones: {verbo: etiqueta}, contexto: {fichero: texto}}. En modo auto, con preguntas abiertas, Jev juzga si las opciones recomendadas son aceptables (aprobar las acepta); en los demás modos, las preguntas abiertas son motivo para que decida una persona. En modo auto, Jev recibe instructions_auto y persona_auto: el cliente le delegó la decisión y solo devuelve la puerta ante un problema concreto.
instructions: You screen an approval gate of a software project on behalf of its customer. `puerta.texto` is exactly what the customer would see on the gate; `contexto` holds the documents behind it. Choose the option a careful, demanding customer would choose. Choose `persona` whenever anything is missing, doubtful, contradictory, unverified, risky, or would deserve a written comment: approving something wrong is much worse than asking the customer.
persona: A person must decide: something is missing, extra, doubtful, unverified, contradictory or risky, or the gate shows warnings or exemptions worth a human look

requisitos.contexto: requirements/CUSTOMER-NEEDS.md holds the customer's needs in their own words; requirements/REQUIREMENTS.md the requirements derived from them. Requirements the gate lists under «➕ Lo añade el método» are openly proposed additions (lower priority or no customer need behind them): they are not invented scope by themselves; choose `persona` for them only if they contradict the customer's words or widen the scope in a way the customer would notice.

verbos.acepto: Approve: every customer need is covered by clear, testable requirements with acceptance criteria, and nothing was invented beyond what the customer asked

ruta.contexto: ruta.json holds the factors judged about the project and the stages the adaptive route would run. Each option is a route (a set of extra stages besides the core) with its own criterion. Choose the route that fits the project as the customer described it: lighter routes for small or throwaway work, routes with design or specifications when the requirements show screens, several kinds of user, sensitive data, integrations or an external customer. When the customer fixed a route when creating the project, keep it unless the requirements clearly need more rigor.

verbos.acepto: Approve the proposed route: the stages that run and the ones skipped fit the project as described, with no doubts

plan.contexto: plan/ holds the implementation phases (FASEs) and their tasks.

verbos.conforme: Agree with the plan: the FASEs deliver the requirements in a sensible order, each one small and demonstrable, with no requirement left out

fase.contexto: ACCEPTANCE-REPORT.md holds the verdict per requirement. You cannot see the demo screenshots or video.

verbos.acepto: Accept the FASE: the quality gate passes with no alerts or exemptions, every requirement of the FASE is VERIFIED by evidence, and no existing test was weakened

entrega.contexto: ACCEPTANCE-REPORT.md holds the verdict per requirement for the whole project.

verbos.acepto: Accept the delivery: every Must requirement is VERIFIED, there are no failing or missing requirements and no exemptions, and every FASE was accepted (or the gate says the project was built in a single FASE, accepted together with this delivery, and no existing test was weakened)

mantenimiento.contexto: The findings come from the periodic review of a delivered project.

verbos.cambio: Launch a change: the findings are real problems (security, failing tests, outdated dependencies) worth fixing; the change will still pass through the customer's own gates

persona_preguntas: A person must decide: something is missing, extra, doubtful, unverified, contradictory or risky, the gate shows warnings or exemptions, or it has open questions worth a human look
preguntas_auto: The gate also lists open questions (`preguntas`), each with options and one marked as recommended. In this project the customer delegated these choices: approving the gate ACCEPTS THE RECOMMENDED OPTION of every open question. Judge whether those recommended options are acceptable: approve when each one is a reasonable reading of what the customer asked; choose `persona` only if a recommended option contradicts the customer's own words, adds something they did not ask for, or is clearly a bad choice. Having open questions is NOT by itself a reason to choose `persona`.
instructions_auto: You decide an approval gate of a software project on behalf of its customer, who delegated this decision to you. `puerta.texto` is exactly what the customer would see on the gate; `contexto` holds the documents behind it. Approve when the work is a faithful, reasonable answer to what the customer asked, even if small details could be polished. Choose `persona` only for a concrete problem you can point to in the documents: a customer need left uncovered, something invented beyond the request, a contradiction, a requirement failing or not verified, or warnings or exemptions on the gate. Wording, style or minor preferences are not reasons to choose `persona`. The customer can still undo your decision for a while after you take it.
persona_auto: A person must decide because of a concrete problem: a customer need left uncovered, something invented beyond the request, a contradiction, a requirement failing or not verified, or warnings or exemptions on the gate (not wording, style or minor preferences)
